population.definition: Population of the Capital District of Bamako (comprising six urban communes: Communes I through VI) recorded in the 4th General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-4, April 2009) conducted by the Institut National de la Statistique (INSTAT) of Mali, tabulated via CityPopulation. Provisional results of the 2022 5th General Census (RGPH-5) enumerate 4,227,569 residents, reflecting the city doubling its population in thirteen years.

source.title: Mali: Regions, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2009 / 2022)

facts.claim: Originally a cluster of Bozo and Bambara fishing and agricultural villages along the Niger River ('Bama-ko', meaning 'crocodile pond'), Bamako became the capital of French Sudan in 1908.

source.title: Mali: Regions, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2009 / 2022)
source.quote: Bamako made capital of French Sudan in 1908

facts.claim: The Musée National du Mali, housed in award-winning local cut-stone architecture designed by Jean-Loup Pivin, safeguards masterworks of Dogon statuary, Bozo puppets, prehistoric textiles, and musical harps.

source.title: Le Musée National du Mali: Architecture de terre et trésors du Niger
source.publisher: Ministère de l'Artisanat, de la Culture, de l'Industrie Hôtelière et du Tourisme du Mali
source.quote: Musée national d'architecture en terre crue et pierre abritant les trésors artistiques du Mali

facts.claim: Grand Marché Dabanani in central Bamako is the commercial heart of the Sahelian metropolis, renowned for hand-dyed indigo fabrics, authentic Bogolan mud-cloth, and herbal traditional medicines.

source.title: Mali: Regions, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2009 / 2022)
source.quote: Grand Marché Dabanani carrefour des tissus bogolan et de l'artisanat sahélien
